uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.

The `sendAddGuestsEmails` function does not check the `disableStandardEmails` flags in the `EventType` metadata, which may result in sending emails to hosts/attendees even when standard emails are disabled for the event type.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:158 — Calendar/video updates use the calling user's credentials (getUsersCredentials(ctx.user) + new EventManager({...user})) instead of the booking organizer's, so when a team admin or attendee triggers it, the organizer's calendar event and references can't be updated and external calendars diverge from the DB; the organizer's user.credentials fetched on line 38 are unused

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the mutation is explicitly allowed for non-organizers (team admin/owner or an attendee). However, the calendar sync step builds the EventManager with the *calling* user (`const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` and `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials })`), not the booking organizer. If the caller is not the organizer, their credentials may not correspond to the calendar that owns the booking, so `updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` can fail to update the organizer’s external calendar even though the DB attendees were already updated. This is reinforced by the fact that the booking query includes `user: { include: { credentials: true } }` but those organizer credentials are never used, which strongly suggests the intended credentials source was the booking’s organizer, not the caller.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:165 — eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees is called but no change to EventManager exists in the diff; unless it already exists upstream, this fails to compile

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `addGuests.handler.ts` calling `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`, but the diff does not include `@calcom/core/EventManager` implementation. Whether this compiles depends on existing upstream code (the method may already exist). Since the absence of an `EventManager` change in this diff does not prove the method is missing, the finding is speculative and not a verifiable defect from the provided changes alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:44 — No check on booking.status or end time, so guests can be added to cancelled, rejected, or past bookings and receive a CONFIRMED .ics invite for a dead event

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the handler fetches the booking and unconditionally updates `booking.attendees` and then constructs a `CalendarEvent` using `booking.startTime`/`booking.endTime` and sends ICS emails via `sendAddGuestsEmails(...)`. There is no guard checking any booking lifecycle state (e.g., cancelled/rejected) or that the booking is in the future before (a) mutating attendees, (b) calling `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees`, and (c) generating/sending invites that set ICS `status: "CONFIRMED"` (see the new email templates). So the code as added can add guests and send confirmed invites for bookings that are already ended or not active, if such statuses exist on the Booking model.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:44 — No handling for seated events (seatsPerTimeSlot set but no BookingSeat/seat-limit logic runs), so seat counts can be exceeded

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the mutation unconditionally appends new attendees via prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}}) after filtering duplicates/blacklist, but it never checks booking.eventType?.seatsPerTimeSlot (or any seat availability) before adding. Since the handler later includes seatsPerTimeSlot/seatsShowAttendees on the CalendarEvent, seated-events are a supported concept, and this path can add more attendees than the seat limit allows (no BookingSeat / capacity enforcement is present in the diff).

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.schema.ts:5 — guests array has no max length, letting any attendee-matched user submit thousands of addresses per call, each generating a calendar invite and email (authenticated spam/abuse vector); add .max(n)

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts`, `guests` is defined as `z.array(z.string().email())` with no upper bound. The new `addGuests` mutation then uses this input to (1) `createMany` new attendee rows and (2) call `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(...)` and `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`, which can trigger calendar updates and multiple outbound emails per entry. Since authorization allows any attendee/organizer (and intended team roles) to call it, an authenticated user could submit a very large `guests` array and cause excessive DB writes + calendar/email fan-out. Adding a `.max(n)` (and likely server-side uniqueness too) would mitigate this abuse vector.

adjudication_records.issue_text: email-manager.ts:538 — sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests) is passed the raw input rather than uniqueGuests, so an already-existing attendee whose email is resubmitted is treated as new and receives a fresh AttendeeScheduledEmail instead of the add-guests notification

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, the handler computes `uniqueGuests` by filtering out emails that are already in `booking.attendees` (and blacklisted), and only those `uniqueGuests` are actually persisted via `createMany`. However it later calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` using the raw input `guests`. In sendAddGuestsEmails (email-manager.ts), attendees whose email is in `newGuests` get an `AttendeeScheduledEmail`, while others get `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail`. If the user re-submits an email that is already an attendee, that attendee will be incorrectly classified as “new” (because the raw `guests` contains them) and will receive `AttendeeScheduledEmail` instead of the add-guests notification. Passing `uniqueGuests` would avoid this misclassification.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AddGuestsDialog.tsx:42 — The `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}` template is always non-empty, so the || t("unable_to_add_guests") fallback is dead code and users can see 'undefined: ...' toasts

adjudication.rationale: In AddGuestsDialog.tsx onError, `message` is built as a template literal: ``const message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`;``. A template literal always produces a string, even when `err.data?.code` is undefined (yielding something like `"undefined: ..."`). Therefore `message || t("unable_to_add_guests")` will never hit the fallback because `message` is always truthy (at minimum `"undefined: "`). This also means the UI can show toasts prefixed with `undefined:` if `err.data?.code` is missing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AddGuestsDialog.tsx:59 — isInvalidEmail is only cleared by the Cancel button; closing via overlay/Escape (onOpenChange) or a successful add leaves the error banner and stale emails for the next open

adjudication.rationale: In AddGuestsDialog, `isInvalidEmail` is set to `true` on validation failure in `handleAdd`, but it is only reset to `false` in the Cancel button handler. The dialog can be closed via `Dialog`'s `onOpenChange={setIsOpenDialog}` (overlay click / Escape), which does not reset `isInvalidEmail` (or `multiEmailValue`). Also, the mutation `onSuccess` closes the dialog and resets `multiEmailValue` to `[""]` but does not reset `isInvalidEmail`, so if the user previously triggered the invalid banner and then successfully adds guests, the banner state will remain `true` and will show again on next open. The claim about stale emails after a successful add is not accurate because `onSuccess` clears `multiEmailValue`, but stale values do persist when closing via overlay/Escape.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:92 — Read-then-write is not transactional; two concurrent requests adding the same email both pass the uniqueness filter and both insert

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the code reads current attendees (prisma.booking.findFirst include attendees) and computes `uniqueGuests` by filtering against that snapshot, then later performs a separate `prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...)`. There is no transaction or atomic upsert/unique constraint handling shown here, so two concurrent requests can both observe that an email is not yet in `booking.attendees` and both proceed to `createMany` for the same email. That creates a classic read-then-write race (either duplicates if allowed, or an unhandled DB constraint error if a unique index exists).

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:170 — Email failure is swallowed with console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails") and the error object is discarded; use logger.error with err so failures are diagnosable

adjudication.rationale: In packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts, the call to sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests) is wrapped in a try/catch that catches `err` but then only does `console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails")` without logging/including `err`. This discards the error details (message/stack), making email-send failures hard to diagnose. The behavior is directly present in the diff and not speculative.

adjudication_records.issue_text: email-manager.ts:531 — Team-member notifications iterate calendarEvent.team?.members, but the handler never populates evt.team, so other hosts on team/collective bookings are never notified of new guests

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `sendAddGuestsEmails` (email-manager.ts) the code sends an organizer email, then conditionally sends additional organizer emails by iterating `calendarEvent.team?.members`. But in the new `addGuestsHandler` the constructed `evt: CalendarEvent` does not include any `team` field at all (it only sets organizer, attendees, uid, location, etc.). Therefore `calendarEvent.team` will be `undefined` after `formatCalEvent(calEvent)`, so the loop over team members will never run and only the single organizer email will be sent, meaning other team members won’t be notified via that path.

This introduces an untranslated UI string and is directly verifiable in the diff.

A claim of “no tests” is not a verifiable defect from this diff alone; it’s a process/coverage suggestion rather than a concrete bug/security/correctness issue demonstrated in the changes.
